title: Dashboards
summary: How a dashboard shows data. The top row loads the dashboard document from Laravel, which decides who may open it. The bottom row is each panel fetching its own readings: Laravel only authorizes and forwards, the Go runtime answers from its own schema. Nothing is pushed; panels poll at the dashboard's refresh rate.

boxes.label: Viewer
boxes.detail: A member of the organization. Range, time zone and refresh interval live in the URL, so a link reopens the same view.

boxes.label: Dashboard workspace
boxes.detail: Loads one dashboard document and renders its widgets on a grid. Edits stay in a local draft until Save dashboard. The view defaults to the last six hours, browser time and a five-second refresh.

boxes.label: DashboardController
boxes.detail: Library, show, save, archive, star, duplicate, versions and access under one route group. Opening a dashboard records the viewer's last viewed time without changing the dashboard's revision. The response carries the widgets, the viewer's abilities and any devices of its panels that have moved to another organization.

boxes.label: DashboardAccess
boxes.detail: Dashboard.view is the floor and Dashboard.manage allows everything. Otherwise the creator owns the dashboard, an organization dashboard opens for everyone with view, and a restricted one only for people it is shared with, directly or through a role. A share grants view or edit, never share or delete.

boxes.label: Dashboards and shares
boxes.detail: A dashboard row holds its widgets, layouts and viewing defaults as JSON, an access mode (organization or restricted) and a revision number. dashboard_shares has one row per role or member with a level of view or edit. dashboard_revisions keeps a snapshot of each save.

boxes.label: SaveDashboard
boxes.detail: Every save sends the whole document with the revision it was loaded at. DashboardDefinition checks it: twelve widget types, each with only its own config keys, and every source must belong to the organization. The row is locked and the save is refused with 409 if another session saved first or the dashboard is archived. The latest 50 versions are kept.

boxes.label: Panel registry
boxes.detail: Maps a widget's type to the component that draws it and to its editor rules. The time series, state history, colour history and consumption panels are loaded lazily, only when a dashboard has one.

boxes.label: @iot-os/charts
boxes.detail: One EChart component (SVG renderer) plus option builders for time series, timelines and gauges, themed from the design tokens. Charts in one group share a crosshair by time, and a chart scrolled out of view holds its updates until it is visible again.

boxes.label: Panel data hooks
boxes.detail: Each panel asks for its own sources through TanStack Query, keyed by device and parameter so panels showing the same thing share one request. All panels share a queue of four requests in flight. Latest values refetch at the refresh interval; history only for a relative range and never more often than a 4000th of its span; consumption at most every 30 seconds. Polling stops while the tab is in the background.

boxes.label: Device measurement API
boxes.detail: There is no dashboard data endpoint. Panels call the device endpoints: measurements/latest, history, state-history and increase. Each checks Device.view in the organization, so being able to open a dashboard does not by itself grant its data. Laravel adds the organization, the device and the retention limit, and asks for history at observed time with configuration revisions merged.

boxes.label: Runtime
boxes.detail: Internal HTTP behind a shared bearer token. It clamps the window to the retention limit and to now, and returns at most the requested number of points (the portal asks for 500) as bucket averages with minimum, maximum and count. Latest values combine the device's live state with stored values and carry its presence.

boxes.label: device_runtime
boxes.detail: The runtime's own schema in the shared database. Laravel never queries telemetry here for a panel; it always goes through the runtime.

steps.text: A person opens a dashboard in the portal. The time range, time zone and refresh interval come from the URL, else from the dashboard's defaults.
The workspace asks Laravel for the dashboard document: widgets, layouts and viewing defaults.
Laravel works out what this person may do: Dashboard.view first, then manage, ownership, the access mode and any share with them or one of their roles.
A restricted dashboard that is not shared with them answers 403. The library never lists it in the first place.
The document comes back with the viewer's abilities. Each widget is handed to the component registered for its type.
A panel asks for data per source, a device and one of its parameters. Status-like panels want the latest value; charts want history for the time range.
Requests go to the device measurement endpoints, at most four in flight for the whole dashboard. Laravel checks Device.view for each.
Laravel forwards to the runtime over internal HTTP with the organization, device and retention limit. If the runtime is down, the panel gets 503 and the rest of the dashboard still works.
The runtime reads its own schema and returns bucketed points, or the latest values with the device's presence.
The panel turns the points into chart options with the shared builders, and the EChart wrapper draws them.
Nothing is pushed. Each query refetches on the dashboard's refresh interval and pauses while the tab is hidden; an absolute range never refetches its history.
Saving sends the whole document with the revision it was loaded at. If someone else saved first the answer is 409 and the local draft is kept.
